title: Receiver contract
description: What one destination kind requires of a request, and how it answers when it accepts or refuses one. The behaviours every kind shares are in receivers/modes.json. See README.md in this folder. A destination kind's delivery contract: what we send, what counts as accepted, how a repeat is handled and an unknown outcome settled, the evidence it can give, whether it reaches a person, and how its answers are read. backend/tests/Tests/ContractTests.fs checks each field against the code.

kind.description: The destination kind, as in the catalog

model.description: lab: what the fake receiver checks today. confirmed: checked against the CRM's sandbox (RFC-006)

requires.description: Fields that must be present and not blank. A dotted path into a JSON body (inbox_lead.from_first), name[key] for an array of {name, value}, or a form field name. May be empty (a plain webhook requires nothing by itself); a lab receiver URL's ?require=A,B adds fields on top, and a scenario states those with the answer's 'requires'

from.description: Which part of the standard lead fills it

refusesMissing.description: The answer when a required field is missing or blank

duplicates.description: How this kind handles a lead it may have seen, which decides what follows an unknown outcome (RFC-008 §4.3). idempotency-key: ignores a request with a key it has seen. lookup: we can ask whether a record with our lead reference exists. external-reference: stores our reference but does not deduplicate. none: confirmed to have no way to tell. harmless: a second copy costs nothing. unknown: not yet verified against the destination's sandbox; treated at runtime like external-reference or none (RFC-008 §4.3). Every kind is 'unknown' until there is evidence

afterUnknown.description: What follows an unknown outcome (sent, no answer recorded; RFC-008 §4.2). resend: sent again, a second copy is safe (harmless or idempotency-key). lookup: looked up by our lead reference; found settles it, otherwise an operator checks. operator: held as unknown for an operator to check and resolve (found, closed or resent). Follows from duplicates; Dispatch.retryAfterUnknown and Dispatch.runVerifications implement it

evidence.description: The strongest evidence this kind can give that the lead reached the firm (RFC-008 §3.1), and how

handOff.description: person: a person at the firm reads it (it can carry the hand-off and the fallback). record: it stores the lead in a system (the record, which can be late); a person seeing it is not evidence we have. Catalog.reachesPerson implements it

remoteId.description: Whether the destination's answer returns its own id for the record it made: what real reconciliation keys on. unknown until its sandbox shows it

answers.description: How its answers are read. standard: the one table every kind shares (Policy.classify: 2xx accepted; 401, 403, 410 needs reconnection; 408, 425, 429, 5xx and no answer retried; other 3xx, 4xx refused). A kind that needs its own reading adds a value here and the code that implements it

toConfirm.description: What the sandbox must still settle
